evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode = "batched" (functional 43 criteria, polish 6, visual 3; scoring aggregation weighted_mean in functional) and each prompt carries an explicit independence-and-continue instruction. functional/prompt.md line 13: "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion. A failed criterion never ends the session."; line 12: "Never carry a verdict across criteria. Two similar criteria are two checks, and a failure in one must not fail another whose own steps passed."; line 17: "Fail fast: after two failed attempts at the same control or step, stop and fail that criterion, then continue with the rest."; line 28: "give every criterion its own verdict". polish/prompt.md line 12: "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion. A failed criterion never ends the session."; line 13: "Never carry a verdict across criteria ... Attempt every criterion". visual/prompt.md line 15: "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure or low score; return a score for every criterion ... never carry a score across criteria." The only all-or-nothing rule in each scored prompt is the global browser gate (line 5: "The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule in this dimension."), which is the template's own construct and is required by check 29, not a stop-at-first-failure instruction. Every 'stop' in the prompts is scoped to a single criterion (fail-fast line 17, 'retry once, then fail that criterion and move on'). A pattern scan of the criterion text in the three judge.toml files and app_context.md for stop/skip/abort/remaining/other-criteria wording found no instruction that makes one criterion's result depend on another; the single hit (functional/judge.toml line 254, "scored by other criteria, not here") narrows scope and reinforces independence. The wording matches or exceeds the frozen template (template functional Guardrails: "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion."). Counterexample attempts: (a) a broken app failing an early functional criterion: the prompt directs the judge to fail that criterion and continue, so later criteria are still graded; (b) a conforming app with one tool error: 'retry once, then fail that criterion and move on' limits the loss to that criterion. Neither produces a zero-the-rest outcome from prompt wording. Limits: this is a source reading; check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed by me (deterministic rows are reviewed separately), and no configured judge run exists for these bytes. The hosted run on an earlier candidate returned per-criterion entries for 41/6/3 criteria, which is consistent with but does not measure this candidate.
notes: The 'budget exhausted -> mark unattempted criteria failed' rule (functional/prompt.md line 14) and the 900 s polish/visual judge timeouts mean a slow judge can still lose trailing criteria; that is a budget matter for other rows, not a stop-on-first-failure instruction, and is inherited from the template wording.

The frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (sha256 6d44970b...) and rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/assets/WebDev_Rubrics_QC.xlsx (sha256 d7b5d607...) are not byte-identical; I read row 38 from the former. Row 38 wording agrees with quality-checks.md section 38.

Unlike the template, the task prompts do not carry a separate '## Independent scoring' heading in polish/visual; the same instruction is present as a bullet under Evidence discipline, which satisfies the row.
